samples.summary: The new 60-second revalidation loop repeatedly puts the access-granting share token in a request URL, amplifying an exposure the repo deliberately avoids elsewhere
samples.evidence: `resolveShareLink` sends the capability token in the URL path of an unauthenticated GET: `${API}/share-links/${seg(token)}/resolve` (share-links.ts:103). Before this change that happened once per page load. `SharedDocumentByToken` now sets `refetchInterval: SHARE_LINK_REVALIDATE_MS` (60_000) plus `refetchOnWindowFocus: true` (shared-document.tsx:1125-1126), so every open tab writes the token into reverse-proxy/CDN/nginx access logs, APM traces and devtools network history ~60x/hour for as long as the tab lives. The repo already treats this exact token as too sensitive for a URL: `fetchYorkieShareToken` comments "POST with the token in the body (not the URL) so this access-granting token stays out of request URLs and server access logs" (packages/frontend/src/api/auth.ts:190-197) and POSTs it instead. Anyone with read access to those logs replays the token at `/shared/:token` and gets the document with whatever role the link carries — including `editor`. The backend route is `@Get('share-links/:token/resolve')` (packages/backend/src/share-link/share-link.controller.ts:67), so the fix is a POST-body sibling route, matching the yorkie-token endpoint.

samples.summary: revocableDocStore's live pass-through hands out raw data properties and target-bound methods, so anything extracted from the handle before dispose() keeps writing after revocation
samples.evidence: While `isRevoked()` is false the get trap returns `raw` for any non-function (read-only.ts:199) and, for functions, a copy bound to the *raw* target (read-only.ts:202). Both escape the revocation, which only re-routes property *lookups* performed after the flag flips. Concretely: `const d = editor.getStore().doc` while the editor is alive yields `YorkieDocStore`'s live Yorkie `Document` field (it is forwarded verbatim through pageSetupGuardedStore's identical non-function branch, view/editor.ts:3327), and `d.update(...)` writes to the shared CRDT indefinitely after `dispose()` — past both the revocation and the read-only editor the host rebuilt in its place. Likewise `const f = store.insertText` captured pre-dispose stays bound to the raw store. `readOnlyDocStore` closes exactly this door and says why — "Data properties are hidden, not forwarded... `YorkieDocStore.doc` is the CRDT handle, whose `update()` is the documented write path. Forwarding those would have left a wider hole than the prototype one below" (read-only.ts:89-96) — but `revocableDocStore` reintroduces it for the whole pre-revocation window. This contradicts the guarantee asserted to callers: EditorAPI.isDisposed's doc says the handles have "gone read-only, copies already taken included" (view/editor.ts:409-411) and dispose() repeats it (view/editor.ts:4523-4524). No in-repo caller grabs `.doc` today, which is why confidence is low — but the codebase does already read non-function members off this handle (`store.fonts?.ensureFont` in app/docs/docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:496-499), so the pattern is live and the next such reader is a full bypass. Per the repo's own threat model this matters because the server-side check ships disabled by default (`YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE`, packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-auth.controller.ts:100-101, shadow mode at :111-119), making the client gate the write boundary in a stock deployment.

samples.summary: The new revalidation has no staleness bound: any sustained resolve failure — including one the downgraded user induces — preserves the editor role indefinitely
samples.evidence: `isShareLinkResolveFatal(error, resolved)` evicts only on a 404/410 verdict once `resolved` is non-null, and `shouldRetryShareLinkResolve` gives up after one retry. So on any non-verdict failure the view keeps the last good `resolved` forever, and `readOnly = resolved.role === 'viewer'` (shared-document.tsx:195/336/389/439/466) keeps answering with the pre-downgrade role. The adversary in the share-link-downgrade model is the holder of the link, running the browser: blocking `/share-links/*/resolve` (devtools request blocking, a hosts entry, an offline toggle) permanently suppresses the revocation this control exists to deliver, with no upper bound on how stale the cached capability gets. The availability rationale for not evicting on a blip is sound, but there is no compensating bound — nothing degrades the session to read-only after N consecutive failures or after k * SHARE_LINK_REVALIDATE_MS without a successful resolve, which is the fail-safe form of the same tradeoff. Net effect is still an improvement over resolve-once, hence minor; noting it because the surrounding comments present the interval as what "bounds how long a revoked or downgraded link keeps the authority it was opened with" (shared-document.tsx:88-91, docs/design/sharing.md), and that bound does not exist on the failure path.
searchedFor: read packages/frontend/src/api/share-links.ts isShareLinkResolveFatal / shouldRetryShareLinkResolve in full
grep for readOnly derivations in shared-document.tsx (all five: 195, 336, 389, 439, 466)
grep for gcTime/staleTime/maxFailures or any consecutive-failure counter in shared-document.tsx and api/share-links.ts
read docs/design/sharing.md revalidation section in the diff

samples.summary: Internal write paths still target the raw docStore rather than revocableStore, so the revocation invariant the diff establishes holds only because unrelated listener cleanup happens to close them
samples.evidence: `guardedSetPageSetup` was moved onto `revocableStore` precisely so no page-setup-shaped hole survives disposal (view/editor.ts:3318-3321), but the other page-setup writer did not move: `writePageSetup` still calls `docStore.setPageSetup(resolvePageSetup(setup))` on the raw store (view/editor.ts:2325), and it is reachable from the ruler's margin drag (view/editor.ts:2332-2336). `stepSelectionFontSizeImpl` likewise writes `docStore.applyStyles(...)` raw (view/editor.ts:1379). These are unreachable after `dispose()` today only because `Ruler.dispose()` removes its listeners (packages/docs/src/view/ruler/index.ts:460-462) and `neuterMutations` covers `stepSelectionFontSize` — i.e. the revocation depends on two unrelated mechanisms rather than on the store handle being dead. This matters more than usual because on a `/shared/:token` role downgrade the container DOM node persists across the editor rebuild (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-view.tsx:342-359 re-runs on `readOnly` with the same `containerRef`), so any listener that is ever missed in a dispose path writes through a store nothing revoked. Routing these two through `revocableStore` makes the invariant self-enforcing.

samples.summary: MUTATING_METHODS is now the gate for two conditions (read-only mount and disposal) but is still a hand-maintained name list with nothing keeping it in sync, and it fails open
samples.evidence: `neuterMutations` is now the single enforcement point for both `readOnly` (view/editor.ts:4599-4601) and `dispose()` (view/editor.ts:4531), driven by the `MUTATING_METHODS` array (view/editor.ts:1045-1055) whose only protection is the comment "Keep in sync when adding a mutating method." A mutating `EditorAPI` member added tomorrow and forgotten here forwards to the real write path under both conditions, and the gate still reads as complete. This is the exact failure mode the sibling module documents as having already happened once: "a list nobody remembers to extend fails *open*... That is exactly how `MUTATING_METHODS` in `view/editor.ts` came to be missing `getStore`/`getDoc` in the first place (issue #989)" (packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts:10-14), which is why `readOnlyDocStore` inverted to a reader allowlist. I compared the current list against the whole `EditorAPI` interface and found no gap today, so this is about the mechanism, not a live hole: an allowlist of non-mutating members, or a compile-time exhaustiveness check keyed on the interface, would make omissions fail closed the way the store wrapper already does.
searchedFor: read the full EditorAPI interface, packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:51-439, and checked every member against MUTATING_METHODS

confirmed copyFormat/clearCopiedFormat/requestLink/selectImageAt/clearImageSelection/validateCursorPosition/resetAfterDocumentReplace/setSearchMatches/setCommentMarkers/setSpellSession are non-mutating (view state or callback registration)
grep for docStore.<mutator> call sites in editor.ts to find writes reachable outside the api surface
grep for any test or lint rule referencing MUTATING_METHODS

verdict.reason: Every quoted location verified in-repo. resolveShareLink puts the access-granting share token in the URL path of an unauthenticated GET (share-links.ts:102-104), and SharedDocumentByToken now drives it on a 60s refetchInterval plus refetchOnWindowFocus (shared-document.tsx:1123-1126, constant at :93), so the token is written into proxy/CDN access logs, APM traces and devtools history ~60x/hour per open tab for the tab's lifetime. The repo's own policy for this same token class is the opposite: fetchYorkieShareToken POSTs it in the body with the explicit comment "so this access-granting token stays out of request URLs and server access logs" (auth.ts:190-198). The backend offers only @Get('share-links/:token/resolve') (share-link.controller.ts:67-68) — no POST-body sibling exists, so nothing guards this. Tokens can carry role 'editor', so log-replay at /shared/:token (App.tsx:113) yields write access. This is sensitive-token logging, explicitly in the Security lane. The only mitigation (the SPA URL also contains the token) reduces novelty but not the repeated backend-side exposure, and is not a named refutation ground.

verdict.reason: The code is present as described. revocableDocStore's get trap forwards raw non-function members verbatim (read-only.ts:199) and returns target-bound function copies (read-only.ts:202) while isRevoked() is false; the revocation check (read-only.ts:197) only affects lookups made after the flag flips, so any value extracted from the handle before dispose() keeps operating on the raw store afterwards. The escape target is real at runtime: YorkieDocStore declares `private doc` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:577), which is TypeScript-private only, and pageSetupGuardedStore forwards non-functions verbatim too (view/editor.ts:3326-3327), so `editor.getStore().doc` yields the live Yorkie Document whose update() is the documented write path — precisely the hole readOnlyDocStore closes by hiding data properties and says so (read-only.ts:89-96). This contradicts the guarantee asserted to callers at view/editor.ts:409-411 and repeated at 4520-4524 ("even a handle captured before now goes dead"), for the stale-holder-after-role-downgrade threat the repo itself documents (view/editor.ts:4511-4518). I found no guard making it unreachable: dispose() (view/editor.ts:4510-4562) never detaches or invalidates the underlying store/CRDT, and the readOnly construction path (view/editor.ts:1138-1139) does not cover an editor built while writable. The backend context also checks out — the Yorkie auth webhook ships in shadow mode unless YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE=true (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:100-101, 111-119) — so the client handle is the write boundary in a stock deployment. The only mitigation I could find is that today's sole non-function reader re-reads the handle per call rather than capturing it (docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:490-500), which narrows current exploitability but does not close the weakness. In lane (access control / revocation bypass), major impact, no nameable refutation ground.
